# Reviewed SVGR dependency-only derivative

This is not an upstream release. It retains the upstream MIT license, attribution and repository metadata. SOURCE.json pins the integrity-verified npm @svgr/plugin-svgo 8.1.0 artifact and records every original and reviewed payload digest. PATCH.diff records the complete upstream manifest delta: truthful private derivative identity and removal of the unused deepmerge dependency. Every executable byte, type declaration and source map is unchanged.

GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 affects deepmerge 4.2.0 through 4.3.1; no patched release was available during review. This plugin was the website's sole dependency path. Its published CommonJS entrypoint and embedded original TypeScript sources use svgo and cosmiconfig, not deepmerge. Removing the unused declaration eliminates the actual vulnerable package from the resolved installation; no merge algorithm is replaced and no advisory is suppressed.

The website uses a direct file dependency and matching override so @svgr/webpack resolves this implementation. The directory lives under website, so Node resolution reaches website/node_modules for svgo/cosmiconfig even with npm's local-directory symlink. Keep this location invariant. It contains the complete original published payload, not a source package requiring a build script. Install with npm ci --ignore-scripts.

Run node website/scripts/test-security-dependencies.cjs after installing both website and scripts/whatsapp-bridge. It checks provenance, the actual webpack consumer, representative SVGO modes, malformed SVG refusal, qs comma serialization regressions and deepmerge absence. Run the website English production build and the repository's unchanged digest-pinned OSV scanner. Retire this derivative after a maintained upstream release removes or fixes deepmerge and the resolved graph, regression probes and production build pass. Never relabel a vulnerable deepmerge implementation as a fixed package.

qs is pinned to 6.16.2 in website and resolved there and in the WhatsApp bridge. This includes the 6.16.1 advisory fix and subsequent hardening. The website's package-specific release-age exception expires when that fixed release reaches fourteen days; it does not disable vulnerability scanning or global cooldown policy.
